core_concepts: Chapter 8 Categories of Risk I am generally upbeat about AI
However, I am at the same time increasingly concerned and sometimes even scared by the actual and potential problems that might arise from AI
Note, first all of all, that it’s possible to be simultaneously optimistic and pessimistic about AI
Meanwhile, we should at least be clear about the nature and scope of the risks and threats arising from AI
A Classification of Risks Tomes have already been written on the risks of AI
There’s nothing canonical or authoritative about this classification of vulnerabilities
Category 1: Existential Risks For long, there have been fictionalized and cinematic renditions of various AI-induced Armageddon scenarios

In the broadest of terms, the threat under the existential-risk heading is to humanity or civilization—that AI might be instrumental in bringing about the extinction of much of the biological human race or the irrever
Weaponized AI involves the profoundly aggressive use of AI by bad actors (such as aggressive states, rogue regimes, terrorist groups, cyber criminals, or disturbed loners)
Unintentionally devastating AI refers to the possibility of a system accidentally leading to some humanity-destroying event
The notion of destructive autonomous AI perhaps peaked in popular culture in the Terminator movies

critical_qualifiers: I can clearly see the great promise of artificial intelligence as a means of improving the human condition and overcoming some of our gravest social and economic challenges
I can also imagine AI yielding huge efficiency and productivity gains across countless other sectors and industries
However, I am at the same time increasingly concerned and sometimes even scared by the actual and potential problems that might arise from AI
This contrasts, however, with the position of many newcomers to AI—they seem to be allied to one of two camps, one that is indefatigably positive, the other relentlessly negative
A nuanced middle ground seems more attractive to me, one on which we can at least talk sensibly about building beneficial AI while keeping the major threats at bay
Others might choose to slice the pie in different ways or to provide a more exhaustive analysis
Note too that some of the categories overlap to some extent and some issues, such as systems security, can fall under several categories
